research.title: Negation Sensitivity in Textual Entailment Models
bullets: Designed supervisor-guided experiments using paired premise and hypothesis edits to examine how negation placement affects textual entailment predictions.
Compared pretrained classifier responses across lexical overlap conditions, manually reviewing prediction reversals to distinguish semantic sensitivity from superficial token matching.

research.title: Cross-Domain Robustness of Sentiment Classification
bullets: Planned experiments with supervisor guidance to separate vocabulary shift from sentiment distribution changes when transferring review classifiers across product domains.
Evaluated sparse linear and transformer baselines under matched training splits, examining calibration and classification errors involving domain-specific expressions.

work.title: Inventory and Order Processing Support
bullets: Checked incoming deliveries against packing slips, recorded stock discrepancies, and routed damaged or incomplete shipments to the responsible staff.
Prepared order paperwork, maintained organized inventory records, and coordinated routine pickup schedules with colleagues handling dispatch and customer collection.

projects.title: Sparse and Dense Retrieval for Question Matching
bullets: Implemented term-weighted retrieval and pretrained sentence embedding baselines to match incoming questions with relevant entries in a question archive.
Compared ranking quality using held-out relevance labels and inspected retrieval failures involving paraphrases, ambiguous wording, and rare technical terms.

projects.title: Sequence Labeling for Named Entity Recognition
bullets: Implemented a conditional random field baseline and fine-tuned a transformer token classifier using consistent entity labels and train-test partitions.
Compared entity-level precision and recall, analyzing boundary errors and performance differences between common entity mentions and previously unseen names.

projects.title: Extractive Summarization Through Sentence Ranking
bullets: Implemented frequency-based and graph-based sentence ranking methods for document summarization, applying identical preprocessing and summary length constraints across comparisons.
Evaluated summaries against reference texts using overlap metrics and manually examined redundancy, missing context, and sentence ordering in selected examples.
